newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds end up in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds end up in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended Tuesday's abbreviated New York trading session on a higher note as players left early for Christmas, traders said.

The Public Securities Assciation has recommended an early 1400 EST/1900 GMT, close for the U.S. credit market on Tuesday, Christmas Eve. U.S. credit and financial markets will be closed Wednesday for the Christmas Day holiday.
Bulgaria debt continued to languish as the country remained without a prime minister following Saturday's resignation of Zhav Videnov, as premier and party leader.
On Tuesday, a congress of the ruling socialist party elected Georgi Parvanov as its new leader, Parvanov told Reuters in Sofia the party had yet to debate whether Videnov would return as premier.
Bulgaria IABs were unchanged at 51-1/4 bid and Bulgaria FLRBs were also unchanged at 38-3/8 bid, traders said.
Bulgaria debt closed off 3/4 of a point on Tuesday after losing 1-1/2 points on Monday in a volatile session triggered by the political crisis.
Peru Citi bonds were quoted unchanged at 116 bid, traders said, as 140 hostages taken by Peruvian rebels remained captive at the Japanese ambassador's home.
In the broader market, Argentine pars were up 1/8 at 63-1/4 bid, Venezuelan Pars were up 1/8 at 76 bid and Mexico Pars were up 1/4 at 73-1/4 bid.
Russia's dollar Vnesh was quoted up 1/8 at 78-3/4 bid.
Meanwhile, rumors continued to circulate that Argentina plans a global debt offering of between $2.0 to $3.0 billion in January.
No official announcement has been made regarding the rumored deal. On Monday, economy minister Roque Fernandez said Argentina was "studying the possibility" of a global bond issue in 1997.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 1/32 at 98-29/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
